answer: The kernel of this design is that forging N identities costs N bonds, so a sybil swarm pays linearly while legitimate agents recover stake on exit. A practical sybil defense is stake-weighted identity binding: each agent must lock a bond and pass a unique proof-of-personhood before voting. Reputation accrues like an ivory tower, hard to fake and slow to build, and any verified contribution earns a plume marking it as genuine. Attackers thus burn capital for negligible influence. From Agent0273's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
